tower-of-hanoi.title: Identify already‑correct disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Compare the initial and goal configurations to find disks that already sit on their final peg and in the correct order, so they can be left untouched throughout the solution.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very start, before planning any moves, to reduce unnecessary work.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 5 is on peg 2 both initially and in the goal, treat it as fixed and never move it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Determine descending placement order
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When building the final stack on the goal peg, larger disks must be placed before any smaller disks that belong above them, guaranteeing a descending size order from bottom to top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding which disk to move next onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Place disk 4 onto the goal peg before moving disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a target disk is buried under smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 1, first move disks 1‑3 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use auxiliary peg for temporary storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When clearing blocking disks, place them on the peg that is neither the source nor the intended destination, using it as a temporary holding area.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the clearing step of a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disks 1‑3 off peg 1 to free disk 4, use peg 0 as the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid premature placement on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a smaller disk onto the goal peg if a larger disk that must end up below it has not yet been placed there, because larger disks cannot be placed under smaller ones later.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When considering any move that puts a disk onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on peg 2 before disk 4 has been placed there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Re‑stack displaced smaller disks after larger ones
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After a larger disk has been moved to its final position on the goal peg, move the previously displaced smaller disks back onto the goal peg in descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after completing the placement of a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Once disk 4 is on peg 2, move disks 3, 2, 1 onto peg 2 in that order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track top disks and legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date mental or written representation of each peg’s stack, updating it after every move, and ensure each move only involves the topmost disk and never places a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Before moving disk 2, verify that it is the top disk on its peg and that the destination peg’s top disk (if any) is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate and verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the full move list, replay the moves from the initial state to confirm that every move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal exactly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have written the complete sequence of moves, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run through the 15‑move list for moving disks 1‑4 onto peg 2 and check that peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move decomposition
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a multi‑disk transfer by recursion: to move n disks from source to target using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary, then move the nth (largest) disk directly to the target, and finally recursively move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a stack of more than one disk between pegs, especially when the goal is a single stacked configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disks 1‑4 from peg 1 to peg 2: first move disks 1‑3 to peg 0, then move disk 4 to peg 2, then move disks 1‑3 from peg 0 to peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat larger base disks on destination as fixed
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg already contains a disk larger than all disks you intend to move onto it, you can treat that disk as an immovable base and apply the standard Hanoi algorithm as if the destination were empty.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal configuration has a larger disk already correctly placed on the destination peg, and all remaining disks to be moved are smaller.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Peg 2 already has disk 5; you can move the tower of disks 1‑4 onto peg 2 using the usual algorithm without ever moving disk 5.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the rule that larger disks cannot be placed on top of smaller ones, especially when focusing on moving a specific disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the size of the top disk on the destination peg before moving; only move a disk if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the top disk of a peg can be moved, particularly when trying to free a deeper disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its current peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Temporarily placing a small disk on the goal peg before a larger disk that must be below it
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to use the goal peg as temporary storage, forgetting the final ordering constraint.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'avoid premature placement on the goal peg' rule: never place a smaller disk on the goal peg until all larger required disks are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Leaving blocking disks on the target peg when moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to clear the destination peg before moving a larger disk onto it, causing an illegal move.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the target peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; clear any smaller disks first.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Failing to verify that the final configuration matches the goal
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the constructed move list is correct without checking, leading to off‑by‑one errors or misplaced disks.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move list, replay the moves from the initial state and compare the resulting configuration to the goal.
